corpus: All 114 previously frozen archived Codex roots: 73 high-context sessions and 41 below-trigger controls. Selection is unchanged from the archived-root cohort of the 729-session study.
scorer: Deterministic offline heuristic; no local or remote model calls.
hypothesis: An optional keep-score cutoff may preserve more sampled source evidence at the cost of less reduction. Reaching the context target is not required if the cutoff protects remaining candidates.

analysis.disabled_equivalence: Compare baseline and candidate with no cutoff on all 114 inputs; ignore timings and rationale, but require matching plans and probe results.
analysis.paired_retention: Compare each fixed cutoff with the disabled baseline on the same probes. Keep all high-context sessions in the denominator. When a cutoff produces no plan, leaving the source unchanged retains the baseline probes by construction; label these cases as derived.
analysis.controls: All 41 below-trigger controls must remain no-ops under every variant. Controls have no reported literal-probe result.
analysis.failures: Retain failures and no-plan cases in reporting; no numerical exclusions.
analysis.integrity: Check each frozen input hash before and after evaluation and compare verifier severity/code counts.
analysis.default: The cutoff is opt-in for scored only. Existing defaults remain unchanged.

limitations: The same 114 archived root sessions from one person and one Mac were replayed; this is not a new independent sample.

This development comparison reuses an already studied corpus. The original baseline was already known when the three cutoffs were registered before this run; this is not held-out or external validation.
All three cutoffs were registered before outcomes, but none is established as a tuned optimum on held-out tasks.
Literal matching is not semantic importance, correct continuation, task success or automatic recovery.
No provider continuation, billing, local model or remote model was evaluated; this is not a fast-jev-compaction comparison.
No-plan cases remain in reduction denominators as zero. For two high-context no-plan cases at cutoff 0.35, retention is derived from leaving the source unchanged, not measured on a rewrite.
The baseline and candidate use the corrected 64-probe cap. Probe totals differ from the original 729-session study; do not compare their retention ratios as a policy effect.
Structural severity/code counts did not increase; that does not establish safe provider resume.
Timing is descriptive under shared host load, not a latency benchmark.

Private transcripts, session identifiers, paths, per-session hashes, corpus manifests and per-session results are excluded; the exact private corpus cannot be independently replayed from this download.
